heading: `logical: false` and the tick problem
text:
## `logical: false` and the tick problem [LNOG.8]

The "tick problem" [LLOG.3] arises when a time-bound LHS test
(e.g., `now() - t.ts < 30_s`) that supported a logical fact expires
between ticks.  The logical fact remains until the next tick, giving a
brief window where a stale derived fact is live in WM.

Under `logical: false`, the tick problem does not exist: there are no
logical facts, so there is no derived fact that could become stale via
TMS non-retraction.  Facts expire only via explicit retraction or TTL
expiry (which is handled by the TTL tick on the correct cycle).
